name: Capture Monster
body:
What is a Monster?

To a monster trainer, a monster is any creature with a simple aura. A creature’s aura is simple when:

the creature doesn’t have class levels. Creatures with class levels fundamentally change their essence—change what they are—giving them complex auras and, in some cases, changing their physical form entirely.
the creature is not summoned, already captured, or gained through a class feature such as arcane bond, natural bond, or eidolon.
the creature’s CR is equal to or less than the monster trainer’s level. A trainer’s essence may not be strong enough to direct a more powerful monster than her experience would allow, and such monsters can even prove unresponsive or dismissive of the trainer when called upon outside of stressful situations such as during downtime.
the creature has an Intelligence score. Mindless (Int —­­) creatures lack discernible essence and must awaken (as the spell), be commanded by their creator, or somehow be persuaded (food and gentle sounds to coax oozes and vermin, for example) before they can be captured.

School universal; Level trainer 0

CASTING

Casting Time 1 standard action
Components none

EFFECT

Range close (25 ft. plus 5 ft. per 2 levels)
Target One monster
Duration instantaneous
Saving Throw Will negates, see text; Spell Resistance yes

DESCRIPTION

This spell functions as imprisonment, except as detailed here. The subject is drawn into your essence and travels with you. It remains there unless you release it, gift it to another trainer, or a freedom spell is cast on you at the location of its capture with the intent to free it.

If the subject is at or above 25% of its total hits points, it receives a +2 bonus to save against being captured. If it is at or above 50% of its total hit points, it receives a +5 bonus instead.

See ‘What is Considered a Monster?’ above for more details on what creatures are considered monsters by a monster trainer.
